results.reasoning: Driven with node bin/walkdown.js on throwaway machines (mktemp HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME); nothing was served, so port 4771 went unused. The steps hold: a home path registers one blueprint, the repository path lists and marks, no terminal registers nothing without --all or --only, and a path with no home refuses. Both halves of n-0551 are fixed: a re-cloned checkout relearns its .git and survives a later remote change in place, and an amended, gc'd, moved checkout keeps its IDs. A re-clone that is then moved, and later moved again under a renamed remote, keeps its IDs, the last with --project. It fails on inode reuse, which the fix's own comment names. On an exFAT drive ejected and plugged back in, a new .git took the deleted project's inode number. An unrelated repository started elsewhere on that drive then took the deleted project's IDs as moved, despite another first commit; the commit before the fix gave it new IDs. At the deleted project's own path, a repository with another origin and first commit read as already listed, even with --project.
